title: Cherry: Ancient Cherries You Can Visit
meta_description: Three cherries whose exact species is unconfirmed: a 900-year Uda tree, a Fukuoka cherry moved by crane in 2008, and Kyoto's carriage-turning cherry.
intro: Three cherries on this map carry only their genus, Prunus, most cherry trees being finished inside a century, which makes each of these an exception rather than the rule. Uda's Sen'nen-zakura is reckoned at over 900 years old, standing beside the stone steps up to the temple Butsuryuji. Fukuoka's Seicho-zakura was lifted whole by crane in January 2008, root ball and all, an eight-metre tree weighing roughly three and a half tonnes, and set down thirty metres from where it had grown. Kyoto's Kurumagaeshi-zakura, the carriage-turning cherry, takes its name from a story that an emperor's carriage once turned back rather than pass it; the tree there now is a roughly 80-year-old successor, not the original. If you know which of Japan's many flowering cherries any of these are, tell us.
